responsibility: Provides rustc’s LLVM-independent target description and lowering infrastructure. The crate root (`lib.rs`) assembles and exposes the main subsystems, re-exports ABI-facing pieces, and includes helper logic for locating target `rustlib` data in the sysroot. The `spec` module defines and validates the compiler’s target-specification model—`Target`, `TargetOptions`, linker and CRT-object configuration, ABI registries, JSON loading/serialization, and the built-in catalog of platform/architecture/toolchain targets—so the compiler can reason about supported compilation targets and their options. The `abi` module supplies the target ABI and type-layout model together with function-call lowering machinery, turning Rust types and signatures into concrete per-architecture calling conventions and pass/return decisions across supported native and foreign ABIs. The `asm` module describes target-specific inline assembly, combining a shared validation framework with per-architecture register classes, register names and aliases, operand constraints, modifiers, clobber-ABI handling, and reserved-register checks. The crate-wide `json.rs` file adds the lightweight `ToJson` conversion layer used to emit target metadata and related ABI/spec data consistently as `serde_json` values, complementing but not replacing `spec`’s schema-aware target-spec parsing/serialization. Finally, the top-level `tests.rs` exercises crate-level target-spec JSON decoding diagnostics, ensuring malformed or unknown fields in target definitions produce the expected warnings. Together, these pieces make `rustc_target` the compiler component that models target platforms, their ABIs, and their assembly/interface rules so later compilation stages can generate code correctly for each supported target.
